skill.name: github
skill.description: Use the GitHub CLI to work with repositories, issues, pull requests, workflows, releases, secrets, keys, and account settings.
skill.summary: GitHub CLI reference for common repository, collaboration, automation, and account operations.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, not Ruby execution. The SSH public-key example still touches the sensitive ~/.ssh directory and changes GitHub account trust. Additional risks come from state-changing GitHub operations, secret handling, extension installation, and broad push workflows without safety guidance.

remediation.issue: Destructive and state-changing GitHub operations lack approval guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add a rule that merges, deletes, workflow changes, releases, and secret changes require explicit user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Key and secret commands touch sensitive account and credential areas.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users never to expose private keys or secret values, and require explicit file paths before use.

remediation.issue: GitHub CLI extension installation is not constrained.
remediation.suggestion: Require trusted publishers, pinned versions when possible, and user confirmation before installing extensions.

remediation.issue: The quick pull request workflow stages all local changes.
remediation.suggestion: Replace broad staging with an explicit review of changed files before commit and push steps.

content.value_statement: Teams need quick command guidance for routine GitHub work across repositories, reviews, releases, and automation. This skill provides concise gh CLI examples that Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can adapt with user confirmation.
actual_capabilities: Shows GitHub CLI authentication status, login, and token refresh commands.
Documents repository clone, create, fork, view, and list workflows.
Covers issue and pull request creation, review, checkout, merge, and checks.
Includes GitHub Actions run, workflow, log, and rerun commands.
Covers releases, gists, search, API requests, labels, projects, keys, secrets, variables, extensions, and configuration.
limitations: It is a command reference and does not install the GitHub CLI.
Many examples can change remote GitHub state and need user approval.
Examples use placeholders that must be replaced with real repository values.
It does not enforce permissions, confirmations, or dry-run behavior.

use_cases.title: Repository maintenance
use_cases.description: List repositories, inspect project state, clone code, and prepare safe repository changes.

use_cases.title: Review coordination
use_cases.description: Create pull requests, review changes, check CI status, and prepare merge decisions.

use_cases.title: Release and automation support
use_cases.description: Inspect workflow runs, manage releases, review secrets, and coordinate deployment tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect repository status
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this GitHub CLI skill to inspect the current repository. Show authentication, repository details, open issues, and open pull requests. Do not make changes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an issue
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a tracked issue with review before posting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a GitHub issue. Ask for the title, body, labels, and assignees. Preview the action and wait for my confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Review a pull request
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess a pull request before submitting a review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pull request 45 with the GitHub CLI. Check status, inspect changes, summarize risk, and ask before submitting any review.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a guarded release
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release workflow with approval gates.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a release for version 1.2.0. Check workflows, draft release notes, list required assets, and require approval before publishing.

output_examples.input: Show me a safe plan to create a pull request for the current branch.
output_examples.output: A concise workflow with authentication checks, branch review, pull request preparation, and explicit approval before publishing.

output_examples.input: Help triage open issues in this repository.
output_examples.output: A short triage plan with filters, labels, ownership checks, duplicate checks, and suggested next actions.
A release checklist covering workflow status, tag review, generated notes, asset checks, and final approval.

best_practices: Start with read-only GitHub CLI commands before any write operation.
Confirm repository owner, branch, issue number, and pull request number before acting.
Ask for explicit approval before secrets, keys, releases, workflow changes, merges, or deletes.
anti_patterns: Do not run merge, delete, or secret commands without user confirmation.
Do not paste private keys, tokens, or secret values into prompts.
Do not install GitHub CLI extensions from untrusted repositories.

faq.question: Does this skill require the GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The commands require gh to be installed and available in the shell.

faq.question: Can this skill change remote repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. Several examples can create, merge, delete, publish, or configure GitHub resources.

faq.question: Does it manage authentication?
faq.answer: It shows authentication status, login, and token refresh commands. It does not store credentials itself.

faq.question: Can it manage GitHub secrets?
faq.answer: Yes. Treat secret commands as sensitive and require confirmation before using them.

faq.question: Is it safe for public repositories?
faq.answer: Use read-only prompts first. Confirm every write action before changing a public repository.

faq.question: Does it support GitHub Enterprise?
faq.answer: The examples use standard gh commands. Enterprise use may need host settings and matching permissions.
